segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I’ve got the quote in front of me for 48 seats, the calibration tracking module, and the onboarding package.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Main thing is we need this live before October 7. Our audit starts October 21, and I don't want the lab techs learning it that week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Totally. And sorry the revised quote got to you late yesterday. My day kind of got swallowed by typing opportunity notes into the pipeline software, cleaning up duplicate company records in the database, and pulling together the internal approval packet for the discount. It was like four and a half hours of clerical stuff, so I had almost no time left to actually talk with buyers or work through your rollout questions until the end of the day.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yeah, I get it. Just, on our side, finance is asking whether the $18,600 implementation is one invoice or split.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: We can split it. The proposal has $9,300 due at signature and $9,300 on go-live. The subscription is $31,200 annually for the 48 named users, net 30, with a 12-month initial term.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Named users is fine. We might add six QA supervisors in January, but not now. Is there a price hold for those?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, I can add a line that additional seats through March 31 are at $650 per seat per year, prorated to your renewal date. No minimum on that add-on.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. And the service levels, the support response says one business day. Can you make that four hours for severity one issues?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: For severity one, yes. I’ll put four business hours in the order form. Just to be candid, if I don’t get it over right after this, it’ll be closer to 5:30 because I’m blocked again doing pipeline updates, fixing account fields, and assembling the deal desk paperwork for month-end. That admin work crowds out the actual buyer conversations, which is not great, but I want to get your terms right before I send it.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Understood. If you send it today, I can route it to procurement tomorrow morning. They’ll need the vendor tax form and insurance certificate too.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep. I’ll attach the tax form, insurance certificate, and the updated order form with the split implementation invoice, March 31 seat price hold, and four-hour severity one response.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. If procurement doesn’t redline the limitation of liability section, we should be able to sign by September 12.
